summary: Draft is sound: no errors found. Splits, case labels (gender: pitta/viṣa not involved), identifications (pāṇḍuroga, śopha, apasmāra, kuṣṭha, gulma, meha, kṣaya, udara, visarpa, vātāsra=vātarakta, manyā, basti-śiras, anala) are plausible and hedged correctly in English; Hindi lacked a few hedges/glosses (kuṣṭha group, jantu, upadrava, mala, vātarakta, aṣṭhīlā 'stony'), patched. Prognostic statements are translated exactly; nothing softened. Typo flags all plausible and src kept as printed; conjectural marks consistent with the glossary except u63 (nothing substituted, mark removed) and Hindi mark placement in 56 and 80. Issues: 0 errors, 32 minor (patchable and observations). Units needing human decision: 43 (construction, low), 53/54 (construction, possible verb swap), 55-56 (no correlative), 60 (subject kuṣṭha and/or visarpa), 61 (vāyu vs Vāta), 62/63 (garbled, low), 66 (raktī), 75, 76 (locative 'at' supplied), 80 (stimita). No regrouping needed; 65 GROUPING note softened (complete clause by itself).
glossary_suggestions: ānāha = 'bloating with retention' in English, Hindi 'आनाह यानी रुकावट के साथ पेट फूलना'; keep apart from ādhmāna (flatulent distension / पेट फूलना).
aṣṭhīlā = 'hard, round, stony lump' / Hindi 'पथरीली, कठोर, गोल गाँठ' (literally round stone); vātāṣṭhīlā standard term, no modern equivalent.
pañcatā = 'death (literally the state of five)'; Hindi 'पञ्चता यानी मृत्यु'.
jantu = 'creatures (worms or vermin)'; Hindi must carry the hedge: 'कीड़ों या छोटे जीवों'.

'On a conjectural reading' only where a substituted word is adopted in `words`; a damaged stretch left unsplit as 'unclear' carries no mark (p02 ch11 u63). Hindi mark placed at the head of the sentence, not mid-sentence.
vātāsra = probably vātarakta (gout-type); Hindi 'गठिया की श्रेणी का रोग'. visarpa = erysipelas-type spreading skin inflammation (probable). raktī (ch11 u66) unidentified.
udarī = one with udara (belly disease, probably ascites-type): same wording in ch11 u55 and u66.
